title: Architecture review - KV cache prefetch & routing notes (2026-04-07)
content:
Meeting: Architecture review - KV cache prefetch & routing
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 10:00 - 11:15 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-serving-runtime
Owner (note taker): Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha Patel, Jonah Reed, Evelyn Kim, Marcus Li, Priya Desai, Lars Mikkelsen, (joined late) Sara Nguyen

Purpose / Context:
- Follow-up to RFC-142 (KV cache sharding) and recent perf regressions observed on long-context chat workloads.
- Decide on approach for proactive prefetching and routing policy to reduce cold-KV misses without increasing tail latency or cross-shard contention.
- Align on changes to routing layer, telemetry, and rollout plan for Dedicated and Hosted.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Agreed to adopt a hybrid routing strategy: locality-first routing + optional prefetch hints per-request.
- Prefetch will be opt-in at route level (default off for most customers) and enabled automatically for known long-context routes (e.g., streaming chat sessions) via config in Console.
- Prefetching implementation: lightweight async prefetch from same shard when request predicts >N tokens ahead (N = 512 in initial config). Prefetch tasks will be rate-limited and observable.
- We will not change sharding algorithm for this phase; instead add routing-layer heuristics and a prefetch worker pool.
- Action items assigned; plan for a staggered canary rollout with metrics-backed gates.

Notes (detailed):
1) Problem framing and data
   - Jonah: production traces show KV miss rate spikes (4x baseline) for multi-turn chats with injected tools; correlated with increased tail latency on p95/p99.
   - Evelyn: cold-KV misses often happen when conversations jump between routes/models (tool chaining) causing KV state not present on target shard.
   - Marcus: current shard assignment is stable but routing hop (fallback to another variant) causes remote KV fetches that are expensive; these remote fetches are serialized in the critical path.

2) Requirements and constraints
   - Must reduce cold-KV miss rate without increasing p99 latency for other requests.
   - Prefetch requests should be bounded and cancellable; must avoid amplifying load on GPUs when overall cluster is under pressure.
   - Telemetry must show per-route prefetch success, additional network IO, and impact on token cost.
   - Feature should be safe for Private deployments (configurable via private control plane).

3) Proposed designs discussed
   A) Router-level hinting (lightweight)
      - Request includes a hint to router when it expects long continuation (client/SDK sets). Router attempts to route to same shard and schedule prefetch async.
      - Pros: low-latency for happy path; simple to opt-in. Cons: relies on client hints; potential for misuse.

   B) Predictive prefetch (server-side)
      - Server uses history + cheap model/heuristic to decide if prefetch should be triggered. No client change.
      - Pros: transparent to clients. Cons: more complex; false positives could waste resources.

   C) Centralized prefetch worker pool
      - Dedicated worker pool per cluster that performs prefetches to warm KV in shards without blocking the request thread.
      - Pros: isolates prefetch load; can apply global rate limits. Cons: introduces extra hop and more moving parts.

4) Decision and rationale
   - Chosen approach: hybrid of A + C. Start with router-level hinting (A) as the initial implementation to get immediate benefit and gather telemetry. Parallel work to implement a centralized prefetch worker pool (C) that will be used in phase 2 to provide safer global throttling and retries.
   - Rationale: fast feedback loop, minimal risk, easier to roll back. Router hints give customers explicit control (Console) and SDK can be updated to emit hints for streaming chat. Worker pool mitigates amplification once we have telemetry.

5) Implementation notes / tech specifics
   - Router changes (code owner: Jonah)
     - Add optional boolean and prefetch-length-int in request metadata (internal-only header for now).
     - When hint present and predicted sequence > 512 tokens, router schedules an async prefetch job targeted at the chosen shard. Prefetch job fetches KV ranges relevant to the active context window.
   - Prefetch worker pool (code owner: Marcus)
     - Start with small pool (N=4 workers per cluster) and a token bucket rate limiter. Workers run on separate nodes (configurable) to avoid impacting inference lanes.
     - Expose metrics: prefetch_attempts, prefetch_successes, prefetch_latency_ms, prefetch_bytes, prefetch_cancelled.
   - Telemetry and dashboards (owner: Evelyn)
     - New Console dashboard for prefetch: per-route prefetch rate, hit/miss after prefetch, change in p95/p99 latency, and token cost delta.
   - Safety and fallback (owner: Priya)
     - If cluster load > threshold (cpu/gpu mem or prefetch_failure_rate), router will disable prefetch temporarily and fall back to normal routing.
     - Prefetch jobs must be cancelable if the original request completes earlier or changes route.
   - Config/Console (owner: Lars)
     - Route-level toggle: prefetch: { off | heuristic | client_hint }. Default = off except for internal 'chat-long' route which will be set to client_hint for canary.
     - Audit log entry whenever prefetch toggles are changed for Private deployments.

6) Rollout plan
   - Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): implement router hint path + minimal prefetch scheduling (no worker pool). Enable for internal chat-long route on Hosted (canary region us-west-2) and Dedicated test cluster. Monitor metrics and error rates.
   - Phase 2 (weeks 3-6): deploy prefetch worker pool, add rate-limiting, and expand to additional routes on Hosted. Update SDK to emit client hints for streaming SDK.
   - Phase 3 (post-week 6): opt-in Console features for customers; add predictive server-side heuristics (A->B evaluation) if telemetry shows benefit.

7) Action items (owners and due dates)
   - Jonah: implement router metadata parsing + schedule async prefetch stub (PR by 2026-04-14).
   - Marcus: prototype prefetch worker pool design doc + perf budget (draft by 2026-04-16).
   - Evelyn: dashboard prototype with synthetic test results and p95/p99 comparisons (by 2026-04-20).
   - Priya: failure-mode checklist + circuit-breaker thresholds (by 2026-04-13).
   - Lars: Console route toggle UI mockups + audit log spec (by 2026-04-15).
   - Aisha: run a short post-canary retro and produce a one-pager summarizing canary metrics (by 2026-04-30).

Open questions / Risks:
- Client hint adoption: will SDK changes reach customers quickly enough? fallback plan is server-side heuristics but that is higher lift.
- Cost/benefit: prefetch will increase upstream network IO and possibly GPU memory usage; need to ensure cost per token effect is acceptable.
- Cross-shard consistency: prefetch correctness if shard assignment changes mid-request (race conditions). Need to ensure cancellation and idempotency semantics.

References / links:
- RFC-142: KV cache sharding (see linked_artifacts)
- INF-2145: investigation ticket for p99 spikes
- INF-2160: SDK streaming hint proposal
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987 (prototype router prefetch stub)

Meeting notes end. Follow-ups: As assigned above.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- keep prefetch scope minimal to start (context window ranges only), avoid fetching full KV state for entire conversation.
- Watch for burst patterns when prefetch_on_hint flips from off->on for many routes at once (console toggle).
- Consider adding per-customer prefetch quotas in Dedicated/Dedicated+Private to control cost exposure.
